text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, to the saints in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places.
For he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, to be holy and blameless before him in love.
He destined us beforehand to be adopted as his sons to himself through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of his will,

versions.text: In love he destined us beforehand to be adopted as his sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of his will,
versions.explanation: The phrase ἐν ἀγάπῃ ("in love") occurs only once in the Greek (end of v. 4), but it is rendered twice — at the close of v. 4 ("blameless before him in love") and again at the start of v. 5 ("In love he destined us"). One of the two must be removed to avoid adding content. Also, εἰς αὐτόν ("to himself") is currently untranslated.

text: to the praise of his glorious grace, which he lavished on us in the Beloved.
In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of trespasses, according to the riches of his grace,

versions.text: In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace,
versions.explanation: The Greek has the article without a possessive pronoun (τῶν παραπτωμάτων); "our" is an addition, though a common one. Removing it keeps the line tight for reading aloud.

text: which he poured out on us in all wisdom and understanding.
He has made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure, which he set forth in Christ:
a plan for the fullness of time, to bring all things together under one head, Christ — all things in heaven and all things on earth, in him.

versions.text: a plan for the fullness of time, to bring all things together under one head, Christ — all things in heaven and on earth.
versions.explanation: The closing ἐν αὐτῷ ("in him") of the Greek is dropped; restoring it also gives the sentence the emphatic cadence of the original and prepares for "In him" at the start of v. 11.

text: In him we also were given our inheritance, having been destined beforehand according to the purpose of the one who works all things out according to the counsel of his will,
so that we who were the first to hope in Christ might be for the praise of his glory.

versions.text: so that we who were the first to hope in Christ might live to the praise of his glory.
versions.explanation: The Greek says we are to "be" (εἶναι) for the praise of his glory; "might live" narrows this to conduct and adds an idea not in the text.

text: In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and came to faith, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
who is the down payment of our inheritance until we take full possession of it, to the praise of his glory.
For this reason, ever since I heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,
I have not stopped giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers.
I pray that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him,
and that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened, so that you may know what is the hope of his calling, what are the riches of his glorious inheritance among the saints,
and how surpassingly great is his power toward us who believe, according to the working of his mighty strength.
He exercised that power in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places,
far above every ruler and authority, every power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the age to come.
And he put all things under his feet and gave him as head over all things to the church,
which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all things in every way.
